# axm subagents enable

Enable a previously disabled subagent

## When to use

Enable a previously disabled subagent

## Usage

```bash
axm subagents enable [flags] <name>
```

## Arguments

| Name   | Type   | Required | Description                    |
| ------ | ------ | -------- | ------------------------------ |
| `name` | string | Yes      | Name of the subagent to enable |

## Flags

| Name            | Type    | Required | Description                                                                      |
| --------------- | ------- | -------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `--scope`       | choice  | No       | Enable in project (default) or user-level configuration (choices: project, user) |
| `--yes`, `-y`   | boolean | No       | Enable without confirmation                                                      |
| `--force`, `-f` | boolean | No       | Enable even if the subagent has unresolved dependencies                          |
| `--preview`     | boolean | No       | Show what would change without enabling                                          |

Global flags are documented on [Global flags](../global-flags).

## Examples

**Re-enable a subagent you previously disabled**

```bash
axm subagents enable researcher
```

**Preview the change before enabling**

```bash
axm subagents enable researcher --preview
```

## Requirements

None.

## Side effects

None.
